Acquiring Illinois Avenue would complete my red monopoly, but it would cost about $242 to unmortgage and build there. The opponent would not give it away cheaply because it blocks me. They might instead want Mediterranean Avenue to complete their brown monopoly with Baltic.

The opponent might want my yellows or jail cards, but both are too valuable to trade. Dark blue monopolies would be suicide. I am now considering buying Illinois Avenue from them.

I am now calculating the exact cash cost of buying Illinois Avenue from the opponent. It would require about $200 in cash, plus roughly $242 to unmortgage Kentucky and Indiana, and another $300 to build two houses there. That leaves only about $128 in liquidity, which is too little to survive a green rent hit.

Building three houses on the red monopolies would cost $1,350, which I do not have. Even with five houses, the opponent could pay the resulting rent without selling any buildings. Buying Illinois Avenue and building there would also leave me too exposed to survive a green rent hit. This trade is not worth the cash.

Trading away a property with buildings is impossible without first selling all houses, which the opponent would not do. I cannot offer to have them sell their own houses either, since trades only involve properties, cash, or cards. A deal that hurts the opponent is unlikely to be accepted by a smart AI. Completing both monopolies at once would leave me with a weaker brown set rather than a stronger red one.

Mortgaging properties would reduce rent income and is not worthwhile. Trading away Mediterranean Avenue to complete the brown monopoly would cost me its mortgage value and cash, making it a net loss.

Selling the yellow houses would raise only about $225, but it would also slash their rent to base levels and eliminate the liquidity buffer. Keeping them is safer for a possible hit from Atlantic Avenue.

The only viable move is to end the turn. I will keep my strategy private and update my notes. The opponent can only trade Baltic, the Reading Railroad, or the Pennsylvania Railroad because their greens and pinks are blocked by buildings.

Railroad trades are not worthwhile. The opponent would demand too much cash, and a single railroad only halves rent while leaving me exposed to greens. Jail cards might be useful, but they are not the priority.
